```json
{
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "verdict_note": "Narrow pass on visible layout. No hard release blocker seen; fixes 1–3 are small truth/usability items to land before release.",
  "scores": {"DesignQuality": 2, "Originality": 2, "Craft": 2, "Functionality": 1},
  "priority_fixes": [
    {"tier": "should-fix", "issue": "Mobile first view hides most of the data", "detail": "At 375 about 3 of 17 markers are visible and two-thirds of the plot is empty. The axis title 'Last included verification request start · UTC' is off-screen. I see only a text cue, no arrow or edge fade. Pin the axis title and date outside the scroll region, and add a right-edge chevron or fade plus an 'n of 17 in view' count."},
    {"tier": "should-fix", "issue": "Title and intro overstate what the x-axis means", "detail": "'Model results over time' reads as a trend, but everything sits in one ~100-minute session. The only visible disclaimer is small grey caption text. Add a visible line: single session, test time not release date, agreement with assistant-draft labels not independent accuracy. The intro says 'each configuration' while points are model aggregates."},
    {"tier": "should-fix", "issue": "Denominator wording is ambiguous", "detail": "Gemini 4 Argon shows 288 matches plus 36 missing = 324, so the shortfall appears to be missing output rather than disagreement. State that missing counts as non-match. '324' also appears as cohort call slots in the stat strip and as per-model probes; label the units."},
    {"tier": "should-fix", "issue": "Colour claim has no key", "detail": "'Colours identify model makers' but no maker legend exists, and the filter is 'Serving provider'. Add a compact key or drop the claim. The pink and lavender hues are hard to tell apart."},
    {"tier": "should-fix", "issue": "Overlap near 07:05 at 100%", "detail": "Roughly 12 markers are distinguishable in the agreement view and fewer in the completion view. Add a count badge or expand-on-focus; do not jitter x."},
    {"tier": "nice-to-have", "issue": "Polish", "detail": "Use round x ticks (05:45, 06:00…) instead of 05:39/06:04/06:29/06:55. Add the date to detail timestamps. Per-case completion has only four possible values, so lead with '3 / 3' rather than '100.0%'. Capitalise 'invoice matching.' in the detail note. Add space under the mobile 'Inspect configuration' link. Mobile export placement is not shown."}
  ],
  "strengths": [
    "PALO navy/cyan identity is preserved, with a restrained research-chart feel.",
    "No connecting line; the caption says collection order does not measure improvement.",
    "The exclusion is explicit: '17 shown · 1 excluded', with the Fugu Max reason stated.",
    "The selected point has a ring, drop-line, label and a detail panel with raw counts and first/last request times.",
    "Model chips give a non-hover route to overlapped points, and the select shows a visible focus ring.",
    "Exports are easy to find on desktop.",
    "The 'Nov' date format is unambiguous, and UTC is stated."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This is an advisory review of four stills, not benchmark validation; no dates, values or counts were verified.",
    "Stills cannot prove filters, autoscroll, keyboard use, export contents or the absence of JS errors.",
    "The 768 view, mobile chips, mobile exports and the expanded 'Exact values' section were not shown.",
    "Contrast was judged by eye only."
  ]
}
```

reasoning_details.text:
I'm going through the desktop 1440 screenshot now, noting the "Model results over time" header and its "Observed results · Internal tests" eyebrow. The title suggests a trend over time, but the recorded test times all fall within about 100 minutes on a single day, so I'm checking how the caption frames the timing.

Next I'm checking the axis ticks, which are unevenly spaced at roughly 25-minute steps, and the point clusters: a few overlapping markers near 05:44 and a dense group around 07:05. Most of the plot between those two times is empty, and the overlap hides some of the 17 points.

Now I'm weighing the detail panel's numbers: 288 of 324 matches, with 36 missing. Since 36 is exactly one call's share of 324, a single dispatched request may have gone uncompleted, and the 88.9% may be counting those gaps as misses.

I'm now going through the detail panel's labels and the colour scheme, noting that the colours seem to mark model makers but no legend ties them to makers, while the filter is labelled "Serving provider." I'm also checking the model names, which look like fallbacks built from IDs, and the note about the excluded model.

I'm noting that the stat strip's 324 "assigned call slots" is a cohort figure, which happens to match the per-model probe count on the chart, so the same number could easily be read two different ways.

I'm checking the y-axis now, with its "Draft-label agreement (%)" title and 0–100 ticks, and wondering whether the markers at 100 are being clipped at the top edge of the plot.

I'm checking how the tick labels line up, with the x-axis ticks starting at 05:39 and ending at 07:20, and suggesting rounder 15-minute steps would read better. I'm also noting the selected marker's yellow ring, dashed dropline, and leader line, and that the model chips sit in two rows with the first row cut off at the bottom of the desktop view.

I'm checking the completion chart's details: the invoice note, the 100% result, and the 3/3 call count, along with the start times and the zero missing classifications.

Now I'm checking the completion chart's y-axis, where three calls per model only allow steps of 0, 33, 67, and 100, so showing "100.0%" looks more precise than the data supports. I'm thinking the 3/3 counts should be the headline instead, and I'm noting that the chart is crowded, with most of the 17 points stacked at 100.

I'm checking the mobile view now, where the main cluster of points sits off-screen to the right, and I'm wondering whether the swipe text cue is enough without any visible arrow or edge fade inside the plot. I also can't tell whether the y-axis stays in place while scrolling, and the x-axis title with its UTC note isn't visible in that first view, so only the date shows.

I'm also weighing whether the "Select a model below" instruction works when the chips sit far below the detail panel, and whether the spacing between the "Inspect configuration" link and the note beneath it feels too tight.

The disclaimer that these are agreement figures with assistant-drafted labels, not independent accuracy, doesn't seem to appear near the chart, so I'm considering moving it up into view along with a note that the x-axis is test request time rather than release date.

Before deciding, I'm checking whether any of the disclaimers, like the note that this is not a release-date axis or that the labels are assistant-drafted, are actually visible at the chart, since that could be a release-blocking issue.
